(s.k.1) He has done good, etc. And now, etc.—for the opinion of Shulchan Aruch is the opinion of Rosh that haTov and haMetiv are not counted among the three hatovot—for haTov and haMetiv were enacted for the slain of Betar: haTov that they did not putrefy and haMetiv that they were given for burial; and three hatovot must be said besides this—therefore he separates these three hatovot and says in each "He has done good to us," etc., unlike the custom to count also haTov and haMetiv among the three hatovot and consider haTov and haMetiv as two—if so "has done good, does good, will do good" counts as one; therefore he does not say the word "He" and the word "to us" except once for all of them together.

Rather he should say "El every day," etc. And Taz wrote that also the word "El" one should not say but "every day"—for he already said "the King Who is good," etc., there. And Taz wrote in Yoreh De'ah siman 342 s.k.14 and his reason and proof from what we say there: a vow partially permitted is wholly permitted—how? He saw from afar people eating his fruits and forbade them; when he approached he saw his father among them and said had I known my father is among you I would have said except my father all are permitted; and specifically when he exchanged his words from what he said initially—how he began saying all of you are forbidden and finally said I would have said so-and-so and so-and-so are forbidden and father permitted; or said initially forbidden to this one and that one and when he recognized them said I would have said all of you forbidden except father; and since he exchanged he uprooted the vow and since permitted regarding father permitted regarding all; and Ran wrote the reason this matter is called exchange (chiluf): each wants that they not suspect him his intent was to forbid also his father; and each chooses language for himself that hurries to reveal his intent he did not intend regarding father; and some choose to say "all of you forbidden except father"—for if he said so-and-so and so-and-so forbidden except father, since they are many people before reaching "except father" they might suspect him he will finally forbid also his father—unlike when he says "all of you forbidden except father" who hurries immediately after saying the word "all of you" to exclude his father; and some choose the opposite and it is comfortable for him to say so-and-so and so-and-so forbidden except father—for if he says "all of you forbidden except father" then when he said "all of you" behold also his father was included—even though afterward he said except father, nevertheless it is not comfortable that his father be a moment in the prohibition—until here Ran.

If so it is the same here when he says "all of us together sons of the covenant"—it comes out that finally he excludes the gentile worshippers from the berachah; nevertheless initially when he said "all of us together" there was an hour the gentile worshippers were included in the berachah; therefore it is better to say the opposite: "us, sons of the covenant, all of us together."

And the reason according to his explanation, etc.—this refers to the essence of the matter that they say sons of the covenant.

As Tosafot wrote, etc.—for we teach there the order of warning for a murderer that witnesses tell him as written "one who sheds man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed" and he is Israel and son of covenant; and Tosafot wrote: therefore one must say two—Israel and son of covenant Israel—to exclude gentile worshippers who are not liable for killing him; and son of covenant to exclude one who is not Israel—an apostate who is in the category of moridin velo ma'alin—for likewise he is not liable for killing him—until here.

And it is difficult, etc.—for an apostate's law is like disqualified testimony d'oraisa implying if validated, etc.—for there it is written disqualified testimony d'rabbanan are fit for agency of the get by them but disqualified testimony from the Torah one does not send a get by them unless the get was validated (according to one opinion the law is so); and therefore Rama wrote an apostate's law is like disqualified testimony from the Torah and accordingly one should not send a get by him unless validated; we learn even if validated it is excluded from agency—for we derive from terumah as written "take from them" and we expound in Gittin and Kiddushin: as you are sons of covenant so your agents sons of covenant. And the reason we require validation for disqualified testimony—see there in Even haEzer.

And in Gittin, etc.—women, etc., slaves, etc.—for they are fit for agency of the get for they are sons of the covenant; and also slaves likewise circumcised. And Rashi wrote there regarding them "from hewer of your wood," etc., regarding cutting of covenant.

And regarding women see what Magen Avraham wrote siman 187.

For it is praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, etc.—even though they conclude "He will make peace upon us," etc., nevertheless the essence is praise. And in any case it is a mitzvah to answer amen because of the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He that is in it.

The cholam makes a great king—meaning a great vowel called king. A small king—meaning a small vowel; unlike chirik with yod which is also a great vowel.

One should answer amen—for one who hears prayer from the mouth of Israel should answer amen.

Each one as they were blessed, etc.—it should read "from Heaven" and not "from the people of Heaven"—for it is better the language of the verse. And one should emphasize the alef of "from" so it not appear heaven forbid "dead."

אמן משום שבח של הקב"ה שבו: החול"ם הוי מלך גדול ר"ל תנועה גדול' הנקרא מלך. מלך קטן ר"ל תנועה קטנה משא"כ חיר"ק עם י' הוי ג"כ תנועה גדול': יש לענות אמן א"ה דהשומע תפלה מפי ישראל יש לענות אמן: כאו"א כמו שנתברכו כו' כצ"ל מאת ה' ולא מעם ה' דטוב לו' לישנא דקרא. וידגיש הא' של מאת שלא יהא נראה ח"ו מת:
cases.en_plain: (s.k.1) He has done good, etc. And now, etc.—for the opinion of Shulchan Aruch is the opinion of Rosh that haTov and haMetiv are not counted among the three hatovot—for haTov and haMetiv were enacted for the slain of Betar: haTov that they did not putrefy and haMetiv that they were given for burial; and three hatovot must be said besides this—therefore he separates these three hatovot and says in each "He has done good to us," etc., unlike the custom to count also haTov and haMetiv among the three hatovot and consider haTov and haMetiv as two—if so "has done good, does good, will do good" counts as one; therefore he does not say the word "He" and the word "to us" except once for all of them together. Rather he should say "El every day," etc. And Taz wrote that also the word "El" one should not say but "every day"—for he already said "the King Who is good," etc., there. And Taz wrote in Yoreh De'ah siman 342 s.k.14 and his reason and proof from what we say there: a vow partially permitted is wholly permitted—how? He saw from afar people eating his fruits and forbade them; when he approached he saw his father among them and said had I known my father is among you I would have said except my father all are permitted; and specifically when he exchanged his words from what he said initially—how he began saying all of you are forbidden and finally said I would have said so-and-so and so-and-so are forbidden and father permitted; or said initially forbidden to this one and that one and when he recognized them said I would have said all of you forbidden except father; and since he exchanged he uprooted the vow and since permitted regarding father permitted regarding all; and Ran wrote the reason this matter is called exchange (chiluf): each wants that they not suspect him his intent was to forbid also his father; and each chooses language for himself that hurries to reveal his intent he did not intend regarding father; and some choose to say "all of you forbidden except father"—for if he said so-and-so and so-and-so forbidden except father, since they are many people before reaching "except father" they might suspect him he will finally forbid also his father—unlike when he says "all of you forbidden except father" who hurries immediately after saying the word "all of you" to exclude his father; and some choose the opposite and it is comfortable for him to say so-and-so and so-and-so forbidden except father—for if he says "all of you forbidden except father" then when he said "all of you" behold also his father was included—even though afterward he said except father, nevertheless it is not comfortable that his father be a moment in the prohibition—until here Ran. If so it is the same here when he says "all of us together sons of the covenant"—it comes out that finally he excludes the gentile worshippers from the berachah; nevertheless initially when he said "all of us together" there was an hour the gentile worshippers were included in the berachah; therefore it is better to say the opposite: "us, sons of the covenant, all of us together." And the reason according to his explanation, etc.—this refers to the essence of the matter that they say sons of the covenant. As Tosafot wrote, etc.—for we teach there the order of warning for a murderer that witnesses tell him as written "one who sheds man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed" and he is Israel and son of covenant; and Tosafot wrote: therefore one must say two—Israel and son of covenant Israel—to exclude gentile worshippers who are not liable for killing him; and son of covenant to exclude one who is not Israel—an apostate who is in the category of moridin velo ma'alin—for likewise he is not liable for killing him—until here. And it is difficult, etc.—for an apostate's law is like disqualified testimony d'oraisa implying if validated, etc.—for there it is written disqualified testimony d'rabbanan are fit for agency of the get by them but disqualified testimony from the Torah one does not send a get by them unless the get was validated (according to one opinion the law is so); and therefore Rama wrote an apostate's law is like disqualified testimony from the Torah and accordingly one should not send a get by him unless validated; we learn even if validated it is excluded from agency—for we derive from terumah as written "take from them" and we expound in Gittin and Kiddushin: as you are sons of covenant so your agents sons of covenant. And the reason we require validation for disqualified testimony—see there in Even haEzer. And in Gittin, etc.—women, etc., slaves, etc.—for they are fit for agency of the get for they are sons of the covenant; and also slaves likewise circumcised. And Rashi wrote there regarding them "from hewer of your wood," etc., regarding cutting of covenant. And regarding women see what Magen Avraham wrote siman 187. And in any case it is a mitzvah to answer amen because of the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He that is in it. The cholam makes a great king—meaning a great vowel called king. A small king—meaning a small vowel; unlike chirik with yod which is also a great vowel. One should answer amen—for one who hears prayer from the mouth of Israel should answer amen. Each one as they were blessed, etc.—it should read "from Heaven" and not "from the people of Heaven"—for it is better the language of the verse. And one should emphasize the alef of "from" so it not appear heaven forbid "dead."

cases.he_html: מברך בורא פרי הגפן כו': עיין בתוס' פרק ע"פ ובהרא"ש טעם למה נשתנה ברכת המזון מכל דברים האחרים הטעונין כוס שכולן ברכ' בפה"ג קודמין וכאן פה"ג באחרונ' ע"ש ואמרי' סברי מרנן אע"פ שבית הבליעה פנוי שלא לחלק בברכת היין וה"ה בקידוש והבדלה ויש מאיזו טעמים למה אומרים סברי על היין ולא על השכר ומצאתי טעם א' משום שהיין הביא קללה לעולם בימי נח שנשתכר ונתארר בני כנען ע"כ אנו אומרים סברי כלומר תבינו שבדעתי לשתות ובדעתיכם אשתה דלא יזיק וע"כ רגילין להשיב אחריו לחיים:
cases.en_html: He blesses Borei peri hagafen, etc. See Tosafot chapter Eruvin and in Ra'ash the reason why birkat hamazon was changed from all other matters that require a cup—for all of them one blesses Borei peri hagafen first, and here Borei peri hagafen is last; see there. And we say savri maranan even though the house of swallowing is empty, so as not to divide the blessing over the wine; and the same applies in kiddush and havdalah. And there are several reasons why we say savri over wine and not over beer; and I found one reason: because wine brought a curse to the world in the days of Noah when he became drunk and the sons of Canaan were cursed; therefore we say savri—meaning, understand that I intend to drink with your consent I will drink so that no harm come—and therefore they are accustomed to answer after him lechaim.

cases.he_html: שם סעיף ג' עכו"ם אין מזמנין עליו ואפילו גר שמל ולא טבל אין מזמנין עליו. נ"ב עיין במג"א מ"ש כל שלא טבל כראוי כמ"ש ביו"ד סי' קכ"ד סעיף ב'. ולפענ"ד אין ראיה דבשלמא התם לחומרא לכך כל שלא טבל כראוי עושה יי"נ אבל כאן כיון דמן התורה מחוייב בזימון אף דמדרבנן לא הוי טבילה מכל מקום כיון דמן התורה הוי גר ומן התורה חייבין בבהמ"ז מצטרפין ולא גרע גם בזה מכותי שמזמנין עליו והיינו כגון אם לא טבל לפני ג' דמפורש ביו"ד סי' רס"ח דלהרי"ף והרמב"ם פסול מכל מקום כיון דהוי רק מדרבנן דהרי מודים דבניו כשרים כמ"ש שם והדבר מוכרח לדידהו מגוף הש"ס דקאמר ר"י מל ולא טבל כאלו לא מל ולמה לא קמ"ל דאפילו (לא) טבל רק דלא הוי בפני שלשה לא הוי גר והרי אם לא טבל לא הוי בפני שלשה והו"ל לאשמעינן רבותא יתירה דאפילו טבל שלא בפני ג' דלא הוי גר. ובע"כ מוכח דאף לדידהו הוי רק מדרבנן ור"י קמ"ל דלא טבל כלל הוי כאילו לא מל ולא הוי גר מן התורה אבל אם טבל שלא בפני ג' הוי גר מן התורה רק מדרבנן לא הוי גר לכך מצרפין אותו לזימון, וראיה ממה דמשני בברכות דפריך שם והנכרי פשיטא ומשני בגר שמל ולא טבל כדאמר רחב"א גר שמל ולא טבל כאילו לא מל וקשה כאן שפיר הו"ל לאשמועינן רבותא ולומר דאפילו טבל רק דלא טבל כראוי נמי אין מזמנין עליו ולמה לי' לתרץ דלא טביל כלל. ובע"כ מוכח דאם טבל אף דלא הוי כראוי מזמנין עליו ודלא כהמג"א ודו"ק היטב:
cases.en_html: There, seif 3. A non-Jew is not included in zimun, and even a convert who circumcised but did not immerse is not included. Note: See Magen Avraham, who writes that this applies whenever he did not immerse properly, as in Yoreh Deah 124:2. In my humble opinion there is no proof. There the law is stringent, and therefore one who did not immerse properly renders wine forbidden as gentile wine. Here, however, since by Torah law he is obligated in zimun, even if his immersion was invalid only Rabbinically, he is a convert by Torah law and obligated in Bircas HaMazon, and may join. He is no worse than a Kusi, who may be included. An example is one who did not immerse before three judges. Yoreh Deah 268 states that according to Rif and Rambam such immersion is invalid, yet this invalidity is only Rabbinic, since they agree that his children are valid. Their position is also compelled by the Gemara. Rabbi Yehudah says that one who circumcised but did not immerse is as though he did not circumcise. Why did he not teach the greater novelty that even one who immersed, but not before three, is not a convert? Necessarily, even according to those authorities, immersion without three is deficient only Rabbinically. Rabbi Yehudah teaches that one who did not immerse at all is as though he did not circumcise and is not a convert by Torah law. One who immersed outside the presence of three, however, is a convert by Torah law, though not Rabbinically, and therefore may join zimun. There is further proof from Berachos. The Gemara asks why it was necessary to teach that a non-Jew may not be included and answers that it refers to a convert who circumcised but did not immerse, in accordance with Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s statement that such a person is as though he did not circumcise. If improper immersion also disqualified him from zimun, the Gemara should have taught the greater novelty that even one who immersed, but improperly, is excluded. Since it specifies one who did not immerse at all, it follows that one who immersed, although not properly, may be included, contrary to Magen Avraham. Examine this carefully.

cases.he_html: טז) על ארופי מברך שהכל ופשוט הוא. ב"י בשם או"ח. וענין הארופי הוא שדורכין הענבים ואחר דריכתן משימין בתירוש עפר לבן ידוע שעה א' או יותר כדי שיציל היין היוצא מהם במהרה ויעמוד במתיקותו ואח"כ מחממין אותו בכדי שהיד סולדת בו. וגם השרביט עושין כן ודעתי מסכמת לברך עליו שהכל וכמדומה שבקושט"א נוהגין כן. כנה"ג בתשו' ח"ב סימן א' י"א שם בהגב"י או' א' וכ"כ הברכ"י או' ב' בשם מהר"א אזולאי דעל ארופי שהוא מי ענבים שנקפא מברך שהכל. וכן הענבים המבושלים הנקרא טראנקופי"ט וכן קאמר"ן די"ן שעושין מהמשמשי"ם מברך שהכל יעו"ש, ועיין לקמן סימן ר"ד או' ס"ג. ודע דיש אנשי מעשה שאין אוכלין הקאמ"ר הדי"ן שמוכרין בשוק משום דידוע דזה שמוכרין בשוק עושין הרבה ביחד ויש בהם מתולעים וגם אפשר שיתהווה בהם יתושים מהפורחים באויר או מן הרומשים באדמה אא"כ שורין אותם במים ומסננין אותם:
cases.en_html: 16) Over arrope, one recites Shehakol, and this is obvious. Beis Yosef in the name of Orchos Chaim. Arrope is made by pressing grapes and, after pressing, placing a certain white earth into the grape juice for an hour or longer, so that the wine emerging from them clarifies quickly and retains its sweetness. It is then heated until it is hot enough that the hand recoils. Sherbet is made similarly. My view agrees that one should recite Shehakol over it, and I believe this is the practice in Constantinople. Knesses HaGedolah, Responsa, volume 2, siman 1; Yad Aharon there, Hagahos Beis Yosef, paragraph 1. Birkei Yosef, paragraph 2, likewise writes in the name of R' Avraham Azulai that over arrope, which is congealed grape juice, one recites Shehakol. The same applies to cooked grapes called trankopit and to kamardin made from apricots; one recites Shehakol; see there. See below, siman 204, paragraph 63. Know that some people of deeds do not eat the kamardin sold in the market, because it is known that market producers prepare a large quantity together, including worm-infested fruit. Flying insects from the air or crawling insects from the ground may also form in it. They eat it only if it is soaked in water and strained.

cases.en_plain: 16) Over arrope, one recites Shehakol, and this is obvious. Beis Yosef in the name of Orchos Chaim. Arrope is made by pressing grapes and, after pressing, placing a certain white earth into the grape juice for an hour or longer, so that the wine emerging from them clarifies quickly and retains its sweetness. It is then heated until it is hot enough that the hand recoils. Sherbet is made similarly.
